content: Hamida Khattabi, an independent consultant based in Rabat, Morocco, contributed to the guidelines. Rossaphorn Kittiyaowamarn, Chief of the Bangrak STI Center under the Bureau of AIDS, TB, and STIs at the Department of Disease Control, Ministry of Public Health in Nonthaburi, Thailand, also participated. Jeffrey D. Klausner, a Professor of Medicine and Public Health at the UCLA David Geffen School of Medicine in Los Angeles, USA, was involved as well. Ranmini Kularatne, a clinical microbiologist at Labtests in Auckland, New Zealand, contributed to the work. Peter Kyambadde, Executive Director of the Most at Risk Populations Initiative (MARPI) and National Coordinator for Key Populations/STI Programs at the Ministry of Health in Kampala, Uganda, was another key contributor. David Lewis, Director of the Western Sydney Sexual Health Centre in Sydney, Australia, also participated. Philippe Mayaud, a Professor of Infectious Diseases and Reproductive Health at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine in the United Kingdom, contributed to the guidelines. Saïqa Mullick, Director of Implementation Science at the Wits Reproductive Health and HIV Institute in Johannesburg, South Africa, was involved as well. Francis Ndowa, a physician specializing in skin and genito-urinary medicine at a clinic in Harare, Zimbabwe, participated in the development of the guidelines. Lilani Rajapaksa, a consultant venereologist at the Ministry of Health in Colombo, Sri Lanka, contributed to the work. Kees Rietmeijer, Medical Director of the Denver STD Prevention Training Center at the Denver Public Health Department in the USA, was also involved. Danvic Rosadiño, Program and Innovations Director at Love Yourself Inc. in Manila, Philippines, participated in the project. Jonathan Ross, a consultant physician at University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust in the United Kingdom, contributed to the guidelines. Anna Shapiro, a Policy Officer at the Global Network of Sex Work Projects in Edinburgh, United Kingdom, was involved as well. Daniel Simões, Strategic Information Manager at Coalition Plus in Lisbon, Portugal, participated in the work. Jane Thiomi, GBV and HIV Prevention Manager at LVCT Health in Nairobi, Kenya, contributed to the guidelines. Jane Tomnay, Director of the Centre for Excellence in Rural Sexual Health at the University of Melbourne in Australia, was also involved. Magnus Unemo, an Associate Professor in Medical Microbiology and Molecular Biology at Örebro University Hospital in Sweden, participated in the project. Bea Vuylsteke, from the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp, Belgium, contributed to the work. Judith Wasserheit, a Professor of Global Health and Medicine at the University of Washington in Seattle, USA, was also involved. Observers included Laura Bachman, Chief Medical Officer at the Division of STD Prevention, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Atlanta, USA, and Azadeh Baghaki, Strategy Manager at Unitaid in Geneva, Switzerland. Lindley Barbee, Clinical Team Lead at the Division of STD Prevention, CDC, Atlanta, USA, also observed the process. Francis Kakooza, Head of the Global Health Security Department at the Infectious Diseases Institute, Makerere University in Kampala, Uganda, participated as an observer. Fernando Pascal Martinez, Research and Development Access Development Lead at the Global Antibiotic Research and Development Partnership in Barcelona, Spain, was also an observer. Tim Sladden, Senior Advisor for Sexual and Reproductive Health at the United Nations Population Fund in New York, USA, contributed as an observer. External reviewers included Henry J.C. de Vries from the Amsterdam Sexual Health Clinic in the Netherlands and Hans Benjamin Hampel from the University of Zurich in Switzerland. Kausar Jabeen, a Professor and Consultant Microbiologist in Pathology and Laboratory Medicine at the Aga Khan University in Karachi, Pakistan, participated as an external reviewer. Monica Lahra, from the WHO Collaborating Centre for STIs and Antimicrobial Resistance at the Prince of Wales Hospital in Sydney, Australia, also contributed. Pham Thi Lan, from the National Hospital of Dermatology and Venereology at Hanoi Medical University in Vietnam, participated as an external reviewer. Ahmed Latif, a public health consultant based in Brisbane, Australia, was also involved. Ioannis Mameletzis, a consultant based in Kyiv, Ukraine, contributed as well. Angelica Espinosa Miranda, Coordinator of Surveillance of STIs at the Ministry of Health in Brasília, Brazil, participated in the work. Koleka Mlisana, Executive Manager of Academic Affairs, Research, and Quality Assurance at the National Health Laboratory Service in Johannesburg, South Africa, was also involved. Lori Newman, a Medical Officer at the National Institutes of Health in Washington, D.C., USA, contributed to the guidelines. Catherine Ngugi, Head of the National AIDS and STI Control Program at the Ministry of Health in Nairobi, Kenya, participated as well. Remco Peters, from the University of Pretoria in South Africa, contributed to the work. Reshmie Ramautarsing, a physician at the Institute of HIV Research and Innovation in Bangkok, Thailand, was also involved. Pachara Sirivonggrangsong, from the Ministry of Public Health in Bangkok, Thailand, participated in the project. Janet Wilson, a consultant in genito-urinary medicine at Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust in the United Kingdom, contributed to the guidelines. The methodology and evidence review team included Maria Ximena Rojas Reyes from the Institut d’Recerca Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau in Barcelona, Spain. The systematic review team for treatment recommendations was led by Nancy Santesso, with contributions from Angela Barbara and Meha Bhatt, all affiliated with the Michael G. DeGroote Cochrane Canada Centre at McMaster University in Hamilton, Canada. The WHO Secretariat and Steering Committee members based at WHO headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, included Avni Amin, Arif Al-Hamad, Kingsley Asiedu, Rachel Baggaley, Magdalena Barr-Di Chiara, Maeve Brito de Mello, Meg Doherty, Sami Gottlieb, Benedikt Huttner, Cheryl Johnson, James Kiarie, Ismail Maatouk, Daniel Marcano-Zamora, Gitau Mburugu, Daniel McCartney, Antons Mozalevskis, Yamuna Mundade, Morkor Newman Owiredu, Anne-Laure Page, Jane Rowley, Özge Tunçalp, Igor Toskin, Annette Verster, Marco Vitoria, and Teodora Wi. Members based at WHO regional offices included Viatcheslav Grankov, Joumana Hermez, Kiyohika Izumi, Agnes Shetty, Ruben Mayorga Sagastume, and Polin Chan.
